desc: Define DP state: dp[parity][sum_offset][product] = reachable, with parity = length of subsequence mod 2; initialize with empty handling and transition by either skipping or taking each element.

Implement transitions: taking nums[i] into an even-length subsequence creates odd-length with sum +x; taking into odd-length creates even-length with sum −x; multiply product by x, capping at limit+1 (sentinel for "exceeds limit").
Handle zeros carefully: multiplying by 0 yields product 0, which is valid (0 ≤ limit) and should be tracked as its own product state.
Choose offset for sums: shift by max possible absolute sum (150*12 = 1800) to index arrays; alternatively use dicts/sets per parity mapping sum → set of products for sparsity.
Write final code: implement DP with per-parity dict mapping sum → set of capped products, seeding each element as a fresh start, snapshotting states per element, early exit when |k| > sum(nums).
After processing all elements, scan all reachable states with alternating sum == k and product ≤ limit, and return the maximum product, or -1 if none.
Verify against the three examples plus edge cases (zeros with k=0 giving answer 0, single element, unreachable k, product exactly limit, overflow-only → -1) and sanity-check complexity.
